title: The Discipline of Computing
description: Historical course, not listed on the current CS catalog page. Introduces computing disciplines to students considering CS or Cyber Security majors or a CS minor.
learning_objectives: Describe career paths and subfields within computing
Evaluate fit for a computing major or minor
source: UA Fall 2024 course record (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://ssb.ua.edu/pls/PROD/bwckctlg.p_disp_course_detail?cat_term_in=202440&crse_numb_in=121&subj_code_in=CS. Historical record: 1 credit. Math coursework/concurrency or placement requirements are not checked by this app.

title: CS I for Majors
description: Introductory programming for CS majors covering basic values, variables, sequencing, functions, branching, loops, and recursion, along with testing, debugging, file-system navigation, and text editing.
learning_objectives: Apply variables, functions, branching, iteration, and recursion in programs
Test and debug programs and work with files, directories, paths, and text editors
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS 100 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Requires qualifying math placement/test scores, qualifying prior math coursework, or concurrent MATH 125, 145, 126, or 146. These math conditions are not checked by this app; consult the catalog for exact thresholds and grades.

title: CS II for Majors
description: Second programming course for CS majors: object-oriented practices, fundamental data structures, computability, problem complexity, and efficient searching and sorting.
learning_objectives: Apply object-oriented programming practices
Analyze algorithm complexity for searching and sorting
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS101 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 100 or CS 110) and (MATH 125 or MATH 145). Only the CS 100 path is modeled; math and the CS 110 alternative are not checked. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Software Design and Engineering
description: Software engineering practice across the program life cycle: systems analysis, software modeling, design theory and practice, testing methodology, team organization, and verification.
learning_objectives: Apply software design and modeling techniques
Practice team-based development and testing methodology
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS200 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisite: CS 101 or CS 111. Only the CS 101 path is modeled. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Data structures including balanced search trees, heaps, hash tables, and graphs, plus algorithm design techniques such as divide-and-conquer, greedy methods, and dynamic programming.
learning_objectives: Select and implement appropriate data structures
Apply core algorithm design techniques and analyze their complexity
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS201 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites also require MATH 301 and specified UA/engineering introductory-course combinations. Only the CS 101 path is modeled; CS 111 and the other requirements are not checked. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Web Foundations
description: Fundamentals of the internet and web page design and development, including HTML, hyperlinks, tables, basic CSS styling, frames, and forms.
learning_objectives: Build web pages using HTML and CSS
Apply basic client-side web development techniques
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS202 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. No prerequisites are listed on the current course entry. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Introduction to Python Programming
description: Introduction to programming and problem solving using Python.
learning_objectives: Write Python programs to solve structured problems
Apply general problem-solving strategies in a high-level language
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS223 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog math prerequisites include MATH 112 or concurrent enrollment in MATH 113, MATH 115, or higher. Math and concurrent enrollment are not checked. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Digital Logic
description: Number systems, Boolean algebra, logic functions and gates, design of combinational logic systems, flip-flops, and design of synchronous sequential systems, with laboratory experiments.
learning_objectives: Design combinational and sequential logic circuits
Apply Boolean algebra to digital circuit design
source: UA undergraduate ECE course catalog, ECE380 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/electrical-computer/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (ENGR 104, ENGR 103, ENGR 123, or MUS 308) and (CS 100 or CS 110). Only CS 100 is modeled; the introductory-course requirement and CS 110 alternative are not checked. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Microcomputers
description: Microprocessors, microcontrollers, assembly-language programming, interrupts, polling, and hardware interfaces, with laboratory experiments.
learning_objectives: Write assembly-language programs for a microcontroller
Interface software with hardware peripherals via interrupts and polling
source: UA undergraduate ECE course catalog, ECE383 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/electrical-computer/courses/. Catalog prerequisite: ECE 380. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Operating Systems
description: Historical operating-systems course, not listed as a standalone course on the current CS catalog page. The current catalog instead lists CS 338, Networking and Operating Systems, and accepts CS 300 in several prerequisite alternatives. Detailed historical content has not been verified.
learning_objectives: Study operating-system concepts; detailed historical learning outcomes have not been verified.
source: UA 2024-25 CS curriculum flowchart (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://eng.ua.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/CS-Flowchart-24-25-1.pdf. Confirms Operating Systems, 3 credits. Current CS catalog lists CS 338 instead; CS 300 is retained for historical completed-course selections. The existing CS 201 prerequisite path is historical and has not been reverified against a course-level catalog record.

title: Database Management Systems
description: Constituent parts of database management: design, creation, and manipulation of databases, including conceptual and relational data models, SQL, normalization, and security.
learning_objectives: Design a normalized relational schema
Write SQL for common data manipulation and query tasks
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS301 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: CS 201 and (CS 200 or MATH 355). Only the CS 200 path is modeled. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Programming Languages
description: Formal study of programming language specification, analysis, implementation, and run-time support structures, including language constructs and non-procedural programming paradigms.
learning_objectives: Compare programming paradigms and language design choices
Analyze run-time support structures for a language implementation
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS403 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 300 or CS 338), CS 301, and ECE 383. Only the CS 300 path is modeled; CS 338 is outside this dataset. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Software Design & Development
description: Modern software engineering practice for reliable, maintainable systems: requirements analysis, software architecture and design patterns, agile methodology, version control workflows, automated testing, and CI/CD. Teams design, implement, test, and deploy a medium-scale software project.
learning_objectives: Apply agile methodology and design patterns to a team software project
Build and operate a CI/CD workflow for a deployed application
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS415 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 300 or CS 338), CS 301, and ECE 383. Only the CS 300 path is modeled; CS 338 is outside this dataset. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Intro to Autonomous Robotics
description: Implementation of robot control software, including motion, kinematics, simulation testing, sensor incorporation, and unmodeled factors.
learning_objectives: Implement basic robot motion and kinematics control
Incorporate sensor data into robot control software
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS460 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 300 or CS 338), CS 301, and ECE 383. Only the CS 300 path is modeled; CS 338 is outside this dataset. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Brain Computer Interface
description: New forms of human-computer interaction based on passive measurement of neurophysiological states, including cognitive workload and affective engagement.
learning_objectives: Explain approaches to passive neurophysiological measurement
Connect physiological signal data to human-computer interaction design
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS461 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 300 or CS 338), CS 301, and ECE 383. Only the CS 300 path is modeled; CS 338 is outside this dataset. Instructor permission is also possible for non-CS majors and is not checked. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Computer Algorithms
description: Construction of efficient algorithms for computer implementation.
learning_objectives: Design and analyze efficient algorithms
Select an algorithmic strategy appropriate to a problem's constraints
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS470 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: CS 301 and either MATH 359 or ((CS 300 or CS 338) and ECE 383). Only the CS 300 / CS 301 / ECE 383 path is modeled. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Formal Languages & Machines
description: Study of formal language classes and their computational models, from regular expressions and finite-state automata to context-free grammars, stack-based automata, Turing machines, and the Chomsky hierarchy.
learning_objectives: Relate regular and context-free languages to finite-state and pushdown automata
Explain Turing machines, recursively enumerable languages, and the Chomsky hierarchy
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS475 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 300 or CS 338), CS 301, and ECE 383. Only the CS 300 path is modeled; CS 338 is outside this dataset. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: High Performance Computing
description: Fundamental concepts of high performance computing, including optimizing sequential programs for modern memory hierarchies, parallel algorithm design, developing parallel programs with MPI, and analyzing parallel program performance.
learning_objectives: Design a parallel algorithm for a computational problem
Analyze the performance of a parallel program
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS481 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/. Catalog prerequisites: (CS 300 or CS 338), CS 301, and ECE 383. Only the CS 300 path is modeled; CS 338 is outside this dataset. Instructor permission is also possible and is not checked. Learning objectives are project summaries, not official catalog outcomes.

title: Capstone Computing
description: Culminating capstone project course integrating skills and abilities from across the curriculum into a comprehensive design and development experience for computer science majors.
learning_objectives: Integrate prior coursework into a comprehensive software project
Communicate a completed project's design and development process in writing
source: UA undergraduate CS course catalog, CS495 (reviewed 2026-10-30): https://catalog.ua.edu/undergraduate/engineering/computer-science/courses/.
